correctness.rationale: Scale to w=1 and set α=π/n, β=α/2. Curvature in the normal angle is the alternating 0/1 wave (each arc has length α in angle, each intervening vertex cone also has length α by the antipodal constant-width relation). Its odd-harmonic amplitudes are 2(−1)^((ℓ−1)/2)/(πℓ). Dividing each by 1−n²ℓ² for the support function and using area=(1/2)∫(h²−h'²) yields the two-copy deficit f(t)=π^−1 Σ_{ℓ odd}(1+cos(nℓt))/(ℓ²(n²ℓ²−1)). To obtain its closed form, integrate the cosine coefficients of g(x)=sin(β−x/n) by parts twice: their unnormalized integral is [g'(π)(−1)^ℓ−g'(0)]/(ℓ²−1/n²). Matching f'' and using f'(0)=0 and f(α)=0 gives f(t)=−π/4+(n/4)[t+(sinβ+sin(β−t))/cosβ] on [0,α]. The three-copy deficit by polarization is (4/9)Σ f(gap)−f(0)/3. If a positive gap is at least α, its derivative is nonnegative while smaller positive gaps have negative derivative, excluding a stationary minimum. For all gaps in (0,α), equal derivatives imply equal gaps or a complementary pair summing to α; a complementary pair would force the third gap to be α, so the only interior minimum candidate has gaps 2α/3. If a gap is zero, even periodicity and nonnegativity give Σ f≥f(0). Independently, the closed form and the triple-angle identity give f(0)−3f(2α/3)=n sin³(β/3)/cosβ>0, ensuring strict improvement over the boundary. At equal gaps the three curvature waves have alternating upward and downward jumps at intervals α/3 and their average has values 1/3 and 2/3, the curvature of (2/3)B_1+(1/3)R_{3n}(1). The support functions can differ only by a first harmonic, excluded by the common center and n-fold invariance. The disk deficit is quadratic in the centered nonconstant part of the support function, hence one ninth of the regular 3n-gon deficit. Substituting the regular Reuleaux area (also obtained from f(0)) gives the exact stated area and the tan expansion gives π³w²/(3888n²). Strict monotonicity follows from d[s tan(c/s)]/ds=tan u−u sec²u<0 for u=c/s>0 in this range.
residual_risks: Equal weights, fixed regular odd order and common rotation center only. Recorded numerical tests are not proofs of rigidity.
